description: Using the magic of big data to enhance agriculture
summary:
**TerraPredict-AI** is a global crop planning platform that helps farmers and agricultural planners understand which crops are suitable for any location on Earth and when they should be planted, harvested, and rotated. Users can select a location on an interactive 3D globe with NASA GIBS satellite imagery to explore local growing conditions. The platform retrieves 60 days of recent climate data from NASA POWER and uses a LightGBM model, trained on more than 40 years of historical observations, to predict climate conditions up to 12 months ahead. It also accounts for global climate patterns such as ENSO and the Indian Ocean Dipole to improve its forecasts.

Using these predictions, TerraPredict-AI evaluates 685 cultivable crop profiles from the FAO EcoCrop database through a seven-stage suitability assessment. It then applies beam search to generate three-year crop rotation plans across three strategies: baseline, soil-regenerative, and water-resilient. By combining satellite data, climate forecasting, and established agricultural models, TerraPredict-AI makes precision agriculture more accessible. It helps farmers make informed planting decisions, reduce the risk of crop failure, improve soil health, and manage water resources more effectively, without depending on expensive soil testing or agricultural consultants.
details:
TerraPredict-AI: Global Crop Feasibility & Rotation Platform

Project Overview

TerraPredict-AI is a global crop feasibility prediction platform designed to help farmers and agricultural planners identify which crops will thrive at any location on Earth and determine optimal multi-year sowing, harvesting, and rotation schedules. Users select any point on an interactive 3D globe or search for a specific location to receive localized agronomic intelligence.

  • Real-Time Satellite Telemetry: Collects the past 60 days of NASA surface temperature, soil moisture, rainfall, solar radiation, wind, and humidity data for the selected coordinates.
  • 12-Month Climate Forecasting: Predicts upcoming monthly climate anomalies using LightGBM models calibrated against more than 40 years of historical observations and live ocean-climate teleconnections, including El Niño/La Niña (ENSO Niño3.4) and the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD).
  • Biophysical Crop Evaluation: Scores 685 cultivable crop profiles—refined from 2,568 species in the FAO EcoCrop database—against local climate, soil, and pH conditions.
  • Multi-Year Rotation Optimization: Generates 3-year crop rotation schedules using a beam-search optimizer across three distinct strategies: current baseline, soil-regenerative, and water-resilient.
  • Interactive Spectral Visualization: Displays six NASA GIBS satellite overlays directly on the 3D globe, covering land surface temperature, soil moisture, precipitation, NDVI vegetation health, groundwater trends, and elevation.

System Architecture & Workflow

The platform operates on a three-tier architecture consisting of a React frontend, an Express.js backend gateway, and a Python FastAPI machine learning service.

  • Offline Data Preparation: The system aggregates over 40 years of daily NASA POWER weather telemetry and NOAA ocean teleconnection indices into monthly statistics. It filters the raw FAO EcoCrop database into 685 rotational crop profiles (incorporating winter ecotypes and cover crops) and trains walk-forward validated LightGBM forecasting models that are only retained at lead times where they outperform baseline strategies.
  • Live Inference Pipeline: When a user selects a site, the backend retrieves 60-day NASA POWER telemetry and passes it to the ML service to construct a 38-month agro-climatic timeline. The engine scores all 685 crops, computes the optimal 3-year rotation schedules, and enriches the top recommendations with verified botanical imagery from Wikimedia Commons before rendering the results in the UI.

Crop Scoring & Agronomic Mechanics

Every candidate crop passes through a seven-gate biophysical filter and a composite ranking model to ensure practical viability.

  • Sowing Thermal Gate: Verifies that current temperatures fall within the crop's viable sowing window.
  • Seedbed Moisture Gate: Confirms sufficient root-zone soil moisture for successful germination.
  • Vernalization Gate: Checks that winter cereals receive their required chilling hours.
  • Cool-Season Cover Gate: Ensures enough cold months exist for proper cover crop establishment.
  • Ripening and Termination Gate: Validates that the final two months of the growth cycle are warm enough for grain fill.
  • Diurnal Frost and Heat Gate: Confirms that estimated minimum and maximum daily temperatures stay within survival bounds.
  • Trapezoidal Suitability Scoring: Calculates a weighted suitability score combining temperature (42%), rainfall (38%), and soil pH (20%), adjusted for soil texture and terrain factors such as clay waterlogging, sandy drought, and slope.
  • Composite Final Ranking: Combines biophysical fit (65%), drought resilience under a 10th-percentile rainfall scenario (20%), and regional agricultural tradition relevance (15%).

Key Platform Benefits

  • Global Reach: Delivers coordinate-specific predictions anywhere on Earth, from the Indo-Gangetic plains to the European Midlands and sub-Saharan Africa.
  • Scientific Grounding: Relies on validated FAO EcoCrop parameters and live NASA satellite observations rather than regional guesswork.
  • Proactive Climate Resilience: Evaluates every crop against 10th-percentile dry-year rainfall scenarios and seasonal monsoon/drought teleconnections so farmers can select resilient varieties ahead of adverse weather.
  • Comprehensive Soil Stewardship: Quantifies living ground cover ratio, biological nitrogen fixation balance, root-residue input, and taxonomic diversity for every proposed rotation plan.
  • Localized Accessibility: Adapts botanical names into familiar regional vernacular, such as displaying "Chickpea (Chana / Bengal Gram)" in South Asia or "Winter Rapeseed / Canola" in Europe.

Mission & Core Objectives

TerraPredict-AI aims to democratize precision agronomic intelligence so that farmers worldwide can make data-driven planting decisions without expensive soil laboratories, private agronomy consultants, or proprietary satellite subscriptions.

  • Reduce Crop Failure Risk: Match crops to biophysically validated climate windows rather than relying solely on historical planting traditions.
  • Regenerate Soil Health: Promote multi-year rotation schedules that naturally maintain nitrogen balance and continuous living ground cover.
  • Bridge the Scientific Gap: Translate complex NASA, NOAA, and FAO datasets into clear, actionable planting calendars for agricultural communities in developing regions.

Technology Stack & Data Sources

  • Frontend Interface: Built with React 19, Vite 8, and Tailwind CSS 4, featuring 3D globe rendering via MapLibre GL, procedural WebGL starfield and sun corona effects in Three.js, and Lucide React icons.
  • Backend Gateway: Powered by Node.js and Express 5 to handle API routing, telemetry fetching, and persistent Wikipedia image resolution.
  • Machine Learning & Data Science: Developed in Python 3.15 using FastAPI and Uvicorn, utilizing LightGBM, scikit-learn, Pandas, NumPy, and SciPy for climate forecasting and biophysical optimization.
  • External APIs & Datasets: Integrates daily meteorology from NASA POWER, spectral imagery from NASA GIBS (MODIS, SMAP, GPM IMERG, GRACE, SRTM), crop parameters from FAO EcoCrop, climate indices from NOAA PSL, basemaps from Esri ArcGIS, geocoding via OpenStreetMap Nominatim, and imagery via the Wikipedia REST API.
